description:
draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §3.3 / §4.3 require onSuccessSetIsDefault to silently ignore an id-not-found or forbidden case ('No error is returned to the client'). The naive shape would be:

  fn set_default_calendar(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Error>>;

…and then the handler/backend would have no way to distinguish 'I changed the default' from 'I silently no-oped'. The SetDefaultResult struct (backend.rs:528-550) makes the three states explicit:

  Result::Ok(SetDefaultResult { new_default: Some(_), previous_default: Some(prev) })
      → changed, prev was 'prev'
  Result::Ok(SetDefaultResult { new_default: Some(_), previous_default: None })
      → changed, no previous
  Result::Ok(SetDefaultResult { new_default: None, previous_default: _ })
      → silent no-op (spec-mandated)
  Result::Err(_)
      → genuine storage failure → handler swallows per §3.3/§4.3

The handler at calendar.rs:328-345 uses this to emit the 'previous default got isDefault:false' response-mutation pair atomically. Without the previous_default field, the swap would be invisible to clients.

This is the right design and survives 'simplify to () return' pressure. The non_exhaustive + Default-impl pattern (with named accessors) also means future scheduling additions (e.g. an OnSuccessSetIsDefaultReason enum) can be added without SemVer break.

DEFEND when reviewers suggest replacing SetDefaultResult with a tuple or with ().
title: set_default_calendar / set_default_participant_identity 'silent ignore' contract preserved through SetDefaultResult
